newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges Croatians to vote in Sunday polls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Croatians to vote in Sunday polls.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday urged Croatians, including residents of eastern Slavonia, to vote in next Sunday's first peacetime elections, saying the polls marked a "critical moment" in the move toward democracy.

The voting for regional councils and the upper House of Counties will include the Serb enclave of Eastern Slavonia, launching its "reintegration" with the rest of the country after a transitional postwar period as a United Nations protectorate. The focus is on former rebel Serbs opting for ballots over bullets.

"The voting in Eastern Slavonia will be particularly important in accordance with the (1995) Dayton (peace) agreement. And for the first time in the aftermath of the Balkan Wars, Eastern Slavonian Serbs and Croats will vote for the officials who will represent them in a unified, integrated government," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
"This is a key step towards national reconciliation...Now is the critical moment to move beyond rhetoric and to consolidate democracy," he told a news briefing.

He said the United States encouraged all citizens in Croatia to participate in the election and specifically urged residents of eastern Slavonia "to stay and take advantage of their rights as citizens of Croatia."
"By taking part in the elections they guarantee themselves representation in the structure and of the future governance of Croatia itself," he said.
He noted that thousands of Eastern Slavonian residents have already registered to vote.
